In 2009, it merged with the Pokémon UK office to create a company that is responsible for "brand management, licensing, marketing, the Pokémon Trading Card Game, the animated TV series, home entertainment, and the official Pokémon website" in markets outside of Asia, as well as managing PokemonCenter.com in the United States. plainText:
The Pokémon Company International (often abbreviated to TPCi) is a wholly owned subsidiary of The Pokémon Company that was first established in February 2001, as Pokémon USA, Inc. In 2009, it merged with the Pokémon UK office to create a company that is responsible for "brand management, licensing, marketing, the Pokémon Trading Card Game, the animated TV series, home entertainment, and the official Pokémon website" in markets outside of Asia, as well as managing PokemonCenter.com in the United States. Kenji Okubo is the current President and CEO.

==History==
 
 
The Pokémon Company International was founded in February 2001 as Pokémon USA, Inc. .

The company's first president was Tatsumi Kimishima (who would later go on to become president of Nintendo) , and on November 16, 2001, it oversaw the opening of Pokémon Center NY at the in New York . 

In 2002 Tatsumi Kimishima was succeeded by Akira Chiba as president. Following threatened litigation, the licencing agreement with Wizards of the Coast for the Pokémon Trading Card Game ended in 2003 . Pokémon USA, Inc. responded by threatening legal action, as they said that the image of Pokémon could be undermined by associating it with cancer. As a result, the gene was renamed .

Up until the end of 2005, the licensing and merchandising for Pokémon outside of Asia was outsourced to 4Kids Entertainment. On December 23, 2005 Pokémon USA, Inc. and 4Kids Entertainment announced that they had agreed not to renew the representation agreement set to expire on December 31 that year, and licencing was brought fully in-house by Pokémon USA, Inc. . This led to Pokémon USA taking over the English-language dubs of all Pokémon animation, as well as several main characters in Pokémon the Series being recast starting with its ninth season.

In 2007, Akira Chiba stepped down as president and he was replaced by Kenji Okubo, previously executive vice president and head of Pokémon USA’s office. In his new role, he was leader of Pokémon’s operations in New York, Seattle and London .

In 2008, Pokémon USA moved production of the English-language dub of from TAJ Productions to DuArt Film & Video. That year, Pokémon UK worked with design agency Red Central to create a marketing style guide for Europe , announced a partnership with Network Distributing to distribute Pokémon the Series and related on in the UK , and announced that (now ) would air the animated series starting from season 11 .

In February 2009, Pokémon USA, Inc. struck a deal with in which their stores would have a dedicated Pokémon Boutique until the end of the year , and in the same month announced a DVD distribution deal with Universal Studios Home Entertainment for Pokémon: Giratina and the Sky Warrior .

On April 9, 2009 it was announced that Pokémon USA, Inc. and Pokémon UK would be unifying their operations under the name The Pokémon Company International. Kenji Okubo said that the rationale behind the move was that the two companies had worked closely together on a day-to-day basis, and that the change in name was done to reflect the connection between the two offices and ensure their worldwide reach 

In June 2023, The Pokémon Company International opened a new office in Miguel Hidalgo, Mexico City.

On February 19, 2026, it was announced that TPCi had entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Excell Brands, a leading U.S. distributor and category management service provider of trading cards and collectibles.
